segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node's classic `EventEmitter` base class (`require('events')`) — not the same thing as the WHATWG `EventTarget`/`Event`/`CustomEvent` trio tracked in [EVENTS-CANCELLATION.md](EVENTS-CANCELLATION.md). Real Node code uses `EventEmitter` pervasively: `stream.Readable`/`Writable` (see [STREAMS.md](STREAMS.md)'s Node section), `child_process`'s spawned handles, and `net.Server`/sockets all extend it.

rows.feature: `new EventEmitter<T>()` / extending it via `class X extends EventEmitter<T>`
caveats: An override's declared signature isn't checked for compatibility against the built-in method it replaces (matching TS's base-declaration-only override checking and this compiler's erased-`as` stance) — a wildly-wrong override signature is the author's problem ([ADR-00631](../adr/ADR-00631.md))
notes: A class in an EventEmitter-rooted tree may **override** any EventEmitter method (`on`/`once`/`emit`/`off`/`removeListener`/`removeAllListeners`/`listenerCount`/`eventNames`) by declaring it — the override wins at every call site (statically and virtually through the vtable), and `super.<method>(...)` reaches the underlying behavior (the nearest ancestor override, else the built-in dispatch), including multi-level `B extends A extends EventEmitter` chains ([TDD-00157](../tdd/TDD-00157.md)/[ADR-00631](../adr/ADR-00631.md))

`EventEmitter<T>` is a compiler-recognized generic built-in (same monomorphized-per-`T` pattern as `Map<K,V>`/`Set<T>`/`Promise<T>`), never itself a registered class (no vtable slot); `x instanceof EventEmitter` answers as a compile-time constant, true for emitters and classes extending one ([ADR-00303](../adr/ADR-00303.md)). See LANGUAGE-CONSTRUCTS.md's `class`/`extends` note

Single inheritance, not composition: a class can extend `EventEmitter<T>` *or* another base, never both — real JS/TS has the same single-inheritance constraint, so this isn't specific to this compiler

caveats: A **tuple** payload `[A, B, …]` is Node's multi-argument event — the listener takes one parameter per element (`(a, b) => …`), [ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md); a non-tuple payload is a single argument (or none, for `void`). No open-ended `(...args)` beyond a declared tuple
A map-typed emitter requires a string-literal event name at every call site
notes: Per-event payload typing via an event-map type argument (`EventEmitter<{ data: string; progress: [number, number]; end: void }>`, [ADR-00303](../adr/ADR-00303.md)/[ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md)); a scalar/`Error` type argument keeps the single-payload-for-every-event form

caveats: Multi-argument `emit(event, a, b, …)` for an event whose payload is a tuple `[A, B, …]` ([ADR-00392](../adr/ADR-00392.md)); a non-tuple payload takes one data argument. Open-ended untyped varargs (beyond a declared tuple) aren't supported
A map-typed emitter requires a string-literal event name
notes: Synchronously invokes every registered listener for `event`, in registration order; returns whether any listener ran
`removeAllListeners()` (no arg) clears every event; `removeAllListeners(event)` clears just that one
`eventNames()` returns registration order (an implementation detail of the underlying map, not a documented ordering guarantee)
Resolved entirely at the `.emit()` call site — no runtime cost when the event name isn't `'error'` beyond the `strcmp` itself
